existingTransitionSource.boundary: The existing allowedTransitions map is the core lifecycle source; it is not currently exported as a typed projection to the desktop evidence surface.

reconciliationFindings: M623 directly proves packaged visibility of the current matrix and preserves the exact no-write/no-authority boundary.

The existing core transition source confirms that lifecycle transitions are implemented behind typed functions, but M623 did not execute or validate any transition and the transition map is not yet projected into the desktop evidence surface.

The packaged observation still does not prove every producer's command batch, approval, execution receipt, authoritative reread, undo/redo, stale/timeout recovery, commit, or aggregate active-GM/Foundry authority behavior.
Stage 11 acceptance remains blocked by distributed lifecycle evidence, not by the matrix's packaged visibility.
remainingGaps: The exact core allowed-transition vocabulary is source-private to the desktop evidence surface.
Cross-producer transition, authoritative reread, undo/redo, stale/timeout recovery, and commit evidence remain distributed across bounded slices.
Broader recovery/cleanup remains separately gated and cannot be inferred from a read-only matrix.
Technical Builder/repository and active-GM/Foundry authority remain distinct boundaries.

decision.reason: M624 preserves direct packaged matrix evidence and identifies the existing core transition map as the authoritative local source, but all four Stage 11 clauses remain partial because no transition or aggregate cross-producer lifecycle/authority evidence was added.
